title: Michael Cohen / Google Bard fabricated case citations

falsehood.claim: United States v. Figueroa-Florez, United States v. Ortiz, and United States v. Amato were real Second Circuit decisions supporting early termination of supervised release.
falsehood.why_false: The Southern District of New York later found that the three cited decisions did not exist.

chain.excerpt: Cohen obtained three purported early-termination decisions from Google Bard and believed the generated citations were real.
Cohen sent the three generated cases and summaries to attorney David M. Schwartz for use in the supervised-release motion.

edge.basis: Cohen's declaration and the court's later opinion describe the citations as originating in Bard and then being sent to Schwartz by email.

chain.excerpt: Schwartz filed Cohen's motion for early termination of supervised release containing the three nonexistent case citations.

edge.basis: The court's opinion states that Schwartz incorporated the cases Cohen sent and filed the motion on November 29, 2023.

chain.publisher: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York
chain.excerpt: Judge Jesse Furman issued an order to show cause after determining that the cited cases did not exist.

edge.basis: The December 12 order directly responded to the November 29 filing and required an explanation for its nonexistent citations.

correction.policy_summary: No correction route has been investigated yet.
